raw.query: WITH unlocked AS (SELECT engine, n_images, mean_ms AS unlocked_ms FROM provenance.collector_encoder_fn WHERE source_path LIKE '%burst_anchor_all%' AND image_px = 448 AND n_images IN (4, 16, 64)), locked AS (SELECT engine, n_images, mean_ms AS locked_ms FROM provenance.collector_encoder_fn WHERE source_path LIKE '%fn_multires%' AND image_px = 448 AND n_images IN (4, 16, 64)) SELECT u.engine, u.n_images, u.unlocked_ms, l.locked_ms, ROUND(((1 - u.unlocked_ms / l.locked_ms) * 100)::numeric, 2) AS pct_faster_at_unlocked FROM unlocked u JOIN locked l ON u.engine = l.engine AND u.n_images = l.n_images ORDER BY u.engine, u.n_images
raw.observed: Unlocked (2887 MHz) vs locked (2392 MHz) speedup ranges 10.05%–18.08% across 6 workload points (compiled+eager × N=4,16,64 at 448px); mean = 14.1%
raw.evidence: DB's only unlocked-vs-locked clock pair (burst_anchor_all @ 2887 MHz vs fn_multires @ 2392 MHz) yields 14.1% mean speedup; 17% is ~3pp above the observed mean and sits at the high end of the 10–18% range.
raw.fix: Rewrite as '≈14% faster (range 10–18% across workloads)' or cite a specific workload point that approaches 17% (e.g., compiled N=16 at 16.5%).
